---
title: "News & Outreach"
subtitle: "Sharing carpenter bee science beyond academia"
---

Communicating science beyond academia is an important part of my research. My work on the behavioural ecology, social organization, and reproductive biology of eastern carpenter bees has been featured through university profiles, research networks, scientific publications, outreach activities, and conference presentations.

## University news and research features

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.tile}
[<i class="bi bi-mortarboard-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>]{.tile-icon}

#### Brock Bee Lab research profile

My doctoral research examined how environmental variation and social behaviour influence maternal investment, reproduction, and social organization in eastern carpenter bees.

[Read the profile →](https://brockbeelab.wordpress.com/lyndon-duff-phd-student/)
:::

::: {.tile}
[<i class="bi bi-award-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>]{.tile-icon}

#### PhD thesis defence

Brock University highlighted my PhD research examining environmental and social influences on foraging behaviour, maternal investment, and mating frequency in eastern carpenter bees.

[Read the announcement →](https://brocku.ca/mathematics-science/2023/11/02/4823/)
:::

::: {.tile}
[<i class="bi bi-building" aria-hidden="true"></i>]{.tile-icon}

#### University of Victoria

Currently serving as a Senior Laboratory Instructor in the Department of Biology at the University of Victoria.

[UVic Biology profile →](https://www.uvic.ca/science/biology/people/instructors/index.php)
:::
